novel_features.name: Engagement diff over time
novel_features.description: See exactly which posts gained likes or comments since you last checked, without re-scraping everything.
novel_features.rationale: Requires local engagement_history snapshots in SQLite; no public Naver endpoint answers 'what changed since last Friday'. Every competing scraper is point-in-time.
novel_features.why_it_matters: When an agent is asked 'which Chilly posts moved this week', this is the one-call answer — no full re-crawl.

novel_features.name: Sponsored-post detector
novel_features.description: Mechanically detects KFTC-required sponsored-post disclosure phrases in the body — 협찬, 체험단, 광고 포함, 유료광고 포함 — and returns a sponsored boolean plus the matched markers.
novel_features.rationale: Korean Fair Trade Commission mandates a finite phrase set for sponsored disclosure; a regex over body_text is byte-perfect. No OSS scraper composes this. Not LLM-dependent.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Distinguishes genuine reviews from paid placements for influencer-audit workflows.

novel_features.name: Influencer health snapshot
novel_features.description: Given a file of blog IDs, returns posts-this-week, median likes, median comments, sponsored ratio, and days-since-last-post — one command, every influencer.
novel_features.rationale: Combines feed walk + engagement + sponsored detector (the press's own composition) over N blogs. Pure local SQL after sync. No Naver endpoint surfaces this aggregate.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Replaces a Friday-afternoon Notion-doc-writing ritual with a deterministic JSON.

novel_features.name: Query bundle (cron-mode)
novel_features.description: Runs a list of keyword/hashtag queries from a YAML/JSONL file, enriches every result with engagement, dedupes by canonical URL, and streams a sheet-ready TSV — one binary replaces the Hermes web_search + web_extract + Playwright pipeline.
novel_features.rationale: Composes search + hashtag + reaction API in one batch with the local SQLite cache. The headline integration story.
novel_features.why_it_matters: The Monday-morning Chilly Hermes cron becomes one CLI invocation with no Chromium dependency.

novel_features.name: Offline Korean FTS
novel_features.description: Korean-aware FTS5 over every post ever cached — title, body, tags, nickname — ranked by FTS relevance and likes.
novel_features.rationale: Korean tokenization in FTS5 with unicode61 + trigram fallback works offline against the local store; no Naver tool ships this.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Rerun the same campaign query weekly without paying for new Naver fetches.

novel_features.name: Hashtag co-occurrence
novel_features.description: For a target hashtag, returns the top N hashtags that travel with it across the cached corpus — the campaign 'neighborhood'.
novel_features.rationale: Local SQL join over posts.tags_json. Korean blog culture clusters hashtags densely per post; no API surfaces co-occurrence.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Strategy signal for campaign hashtag expansion.

novel_features.name: File-driven URL backfill (order-preserving, mixed-format)
novel_features.description: Accepts CSV / JSON column / newline-delimited URLs in any mix of m.blog.naver.com / blog.naver.com / PostView.naver shapes; canonicalizes each; runs concurrent fetches with adaptive rate limiting; preserves input order; emits per-URL error JSON for failures.
novel_features.rationale: The reaction API is batchable, so engagement is O(1) per N posts. The file-driven, mixed-format, order-preserving slice is what no OSS tool ships.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Slack-bundle workflow: paste a column of URLs, get a column of engagement.

novel_features.name: Category browse
novel_features.description: Lists a blog's numbered Naver categories with post counts; --category flag filters feed/local-search results by category number.
novel_features.rationale: Naver-specific (numbered categories are core platform UX); feed JSON already returns category info so this is local query.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Topic-segment an influencer (e.g., only their beauty posts) without crawling everything.

novel_features.name: Comments extraction
novel_features.description: Fetch the actual content of comments on a Naver Blog post — author, body, timestamps, like counts — via the public cbox endpoint. Optional flat or nested-tree output.
novel_features.rationale: The cbox endpoint is public for ticket=blog with the right objectId shape (<blogNo>_201_<logNo>); no OSS scraper documents this — they all either use the deprecated .nhn endpoint or skip comments entirely.
novel_features.why_it_matters: When auditing influencer engagement quality, the content of comments matters as much as the count — bot comments, identical-template spam, or genuine engagement.

novel_features.name: Blog profile metadata
novel_features.description: Get rich blog profile data: subscriber count, daily/total visitor counts, Naver Power Blog status, directory category, profile/cover images — everything Naver shows on the blog homepage.
novel_features.rationale: The /api/blogs/<id> endpoint returns blog-level metadata that no OSS scraper surfaces. Required for influencer-tier qualification (Power Blog, AI Pick, Year of Blog badges).
novel_features.why_it_matters: Influencer-marketing audits need to qualify creators by reach (subscribers, daily visitors) and Naver-assigned tier badges. This is the only command that gives both.

narrative.headline: Every Naver Blog feature the OSS ecosystem has learned, in one Go binary — with a local SQLite store, an offline Korean FTS, and likes counts that match the live page exactly without Playwright.
narrative.value_prop: naver-blog-pp-cli is the read-only CLI for searching, fetching, and aggregating public Naver Blog posts. Phase 1.7 sniffed Naver's public reaction API, so the CLI gets the same byte-for-byte likes count the page renders — no headless browser, no quota, no Naver Developer credentials. A SQLite store and an offline Korean FTS turn one-shot queries into a queryable historical corpus. The `cron` command replaces the Hermes web_search + web_extract + Playwright pipeline with a single binary invocation.
narrative.auth_narrative: No authentication required. The CLI exclusively uses public read-only endpoints: m.blog.naver.com (feed + post HTML), blog.naver.com (PostView.naver fallback), apis.naver.com (reaction API), and m.search.naver.com (search SERP). The Naver Developer API (X-Naver-Client-Id + X-Naver-Client-Secret) is NOT used in v1; if you want to use it as an alternate search backend, set NAVER_CLIENT_ID and NAVER_CLIENT_SECRET (v2 work).

quickstart.comment: Confirm the CLI can reach all 4 Naver hosts and the local store opens cleanly.
Fetch one post: title, body, tags, exact likes (via reaction API), comments — JSON.
List 30 most-recent posts from a blog with engagement metrics inline (one HTTP call).
Find Naver Blog posts tagged with BOTH hashtags (intersect).
What changed in this post's engagement since last week — using local SQLite history.
The headline integration: run a query bundle, get a sheet-ready TSV.
Pull the actual comment content (author, body, timestamps) for a post — the cbox endpoint is public.

troubleshoots.fix: Run `naver-blog-pp-cli doctor --json` to see the failing URL. From Korea this should always work; from non-KR IPs Naver occasionally serves degraded responses — set NAVER_BLOG_USER_AGENT to a Chrome desktop UA and retry.

troubleshoots.symptom: Likes count is 0 when the page shows a higher number
troubleshoots.fix: Your local SQLite has a stale snapshot. Run `post <url>` (without --cache) to re-query the reaction API directly. The CLI never uses static-HTML for likes; if 0 persists, file a bug — the post was likely deleted or set to private.

troubleshoots.symptom: search posts returns empty for a query that has results in a browser
troubleshoots.fix: Naver rotates the integrated-search DOM selectors periodically. Use `--debug-html` to dump the SERP HTML, then file an issue with the dump attached. Until a fix ships, run the query through `feed` against any blogs known to post about the topic.

Naver Blog URLs come in 3 shapes (blog.naver.com/<id>/<n>, m.blog.naver.com/<id>/<n>, blog.naver.com/PostView.naver?blogId=X&logNo=Y). All three are accepted. If the input is a CSV, the URL column must be named `url` (or use --url-column to specify).

troubleshoots.symptom: Sponsored detector misses an obviously sponsored post
troubleshoots.fix: The detector only matches KFTC-required phrases (협찬, 체험단, 광고 포함, 유료광고 포함, '본 포스팅은 ... 받아 작성됨'). Posts that use creative-but-non-compliant wording (e.g., '협업', 'PR') will not be caught — by design, since those are not legal disclosures.

narrative.when_to_use: Reach for naver-blog-pp-cli when an agent is asked to search Korean Naver Blog posts by keyword or hashtag, extract a single post's title/body/tags/engagement, or aggregate engagement across a list of post URLs. It is the right choice when accuracy matters (the reaction API gives exact same-instant counts), when the workflow runs weekly or more often (the SQLite cache compounds), or when the Naver Developer API's 25k-request daily quota or credential requirement is a friction. It is NOT the right choice for write workflows (publishing, editing, deleting posts) or for authenticated-only data (admin stats, 이웃 neighbor lists, drafts) — both are explicitly out of scope.

recipes.title: Replace the Chilly weekly cron
recipes.explanation: Runs the 6 Chilly queries, enriches with engagement, dedupes by canonical URL, writes TSV for Google Sheets, caches everything in SQLite for next week's diff.

recipes.title: Friday influencer health roll-up
recipes.explanation: For each blog ID in the file, returns posts-this-week, median engagement, sponsored ratio, days-since-last-post.

recipes.title: Find what changed in a watched post
recipes.explanation: Compares the live engagement to the most recent snapshot in local SQLite older than 24h. Returns the delta only.

recipes.title: Narrow a verbose post payload for an agent (--agent + --select)
recipes.explanation: Per-post output includes body_text (often kilobytes). --select narrows to just the fields the agent needs, keeping prompt context lean. Pair with --flag-sponsored when scanning a batch.

recipes.title: Find tag neighborhoods for campaign strategy
recipes.explanation: Returns the top 20 hashtags that co-occur with the target tag across the cached corpus, ranked by joint-occurrence count.

recipes.title: Audit influencer comment quality
recipes.explanation: Pulls every comment on a post, narrowed to author/body/time/likes for an agent to scan for boilerplate, bot patterns, or genuine engagement.
